name: Lync
label: K
lede: Three Olympia kids put out four 7-inches and one album on K Records in about two years, then just stopped playing. The members scattered into Beck's records, Built to Spill's touring band and Love as Laughter.

eras.title: A high school radio station and a four-track
eras.text: Sam Jayne and Dave Schneider met in 1991 at their high school radio station, KASB. By 1992, with bassist James Bertram, they were Lync, in Olympia per Wikipedia and AllMusic, putting out singles on tiny labels while K Records watched from the next basement over.

years.cap: Lync, left to right: James Bertram, Dave Schneider, Sam Jayne
years.src: Tone Glow 143: Lync · Wikipedia: Lync · AllMusic: Lync biography · Suicide Squeeze: These Are Not Fall Colors reissue
years.h: Lync takes its name from a bait shop and a video game
years.p: Sam Jayne sings and plays guitar, James Bertram plays bass and sings, and Dave Schneider plays drums.
years.xp:
Schneider told Tone Glow the name came from three places: a bait and tackle store called Linc's near the Lake City Theatre, The Legend of Zelda, and a wish for the shortest name possible. "We wanted the shortest name possible," he said.

Isaac Brock, later of Modest Mouse, played with them for a week or two before the logistics fell apart and Bertram became the permanent bassist. Wikipedia describes the sound as distortion, cryptic lyrics and irregular tuning, with comparisons to Fugazi, Unwound and Drive Like Jehu. Suicide Squeeze calls them a Puget Sound trio that pulled in DC, San Diego and Olympia DIY influences.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lync · Tone Glow 143: Lync · Wikipedia: Remembering the Fireballs (Part 8)
yt: "Turtle", live at the Capitol Theatre, Olympia, May 8, 1993
years.h: Three 7-inches in 1993, none of them on K
years.p: "Firestarter" is a split with Excuse 17 on Candy Ass. "Mhz" (with Landspeed) and "Pigeons" are on Magic Pail.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, all three are 1993 releases; "Two Feet in Front" follows in 1994 on K Records, the label that then puts out the album. Schneider told Tone Glow the first demo tape was recorded that summer on a four-track at a friend's house. Bertram's take on the singles: "Making a 7-inch was just super cool. I felt like we were super lucky."

Tracks from the early 1993 sessions with Pat Maley at yo yo capitol and the late 1993 sessions with Tim Green at the red house end up on the 1997 compilation Remembering the Fireballs (Part 8).

eras.title: Four days with Phil Ek, then nothing
eras.text: Jayne and Bertram turn up on Beck's One Foot in the Grave, and Lync cuts its only album in a Seattle studio. They never announce a breakup; by the end of 1994 they've stopped playing.

years.src: Wikipedia: One Foot in the Grave (Beck album) · Wikipedia: Lync · Tone Glow 143: Lync
years.h: Two of the three members end up on a Beck record
years.p: K Records puts out [[Beck|309c62ba-7a22-4277-9f67-4a162526d18a]]'s One Foot in the Grave on June 27, 1994, recorded in Calvin Johnson's basement studio in Olympia.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists the album as recorded in October 1993 and January 1994 at Dub Narcotic Studio, then in [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]]'s basement. Its personnel list has Bertram on bass and Jayne on vocals, and Wikipedia's Lync article says both performed on it. Neither page says who played what on which track.

Schneider told Tone Glow that on a trip to meet up with Beck, "James broke the stage" at a show in Missoula, Montana. Bertram, on Calvin Johnson: "probably only 26."

years.src: Wikipedia: These Are Not Fall Colors · Tone Glow 143: Lync · Brooklyn Vegan: Lync track-by-track on These Are Not Fall Colors · Suicide Squeeze: These Are Not Fall Colors reissue
years.h: Seattle, four days, and Phil Ek at the board
years.p: John and Stu's Place is the room; Ek, Tim Green, Calvin Johnson and the band share the producing and engineering credits.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the sessions to spring and summer 1994. Schneider told Tone Glow it was the band's first proper studio, and "the whole thing only took four days." The album runs 10 tracks and 42:32, from "B" to the 6:46 closer "Uberrima Fides".

Brooklyn Vegan reports Jayne used a RadioShack-branded Moog and Fisher-Price toys for texture. Suicide Squeeze notes that Ek later worked with Fleet Foxes, Band of Horses and the Shins.

years.src: Wikipedia: These Are Not Fall Colors · Suicide Squeeze: These Are Not Fall Colors reissue · Tone Glow 143: Lync
years.h: Lync's only album arrives on K Records
years.p: These Are Not Fall Colors comes out on CD, LP and cassette. Pitchfork later gave it 8.7.
years.xp:
Pitchfork wrote that it "unspools like a collection of song sketches" that Jayne, Bertram and Schneider "pummeled into working shape." Trouser Press was cooler, calling it "not really good, but far from bad." The A.V. Club praised the ragged ambient loops of spoken-word samples and guitar feedback holding it together.

Tone Glow reports the title came from a school assignment in which Jayne colored leaves blue and black instead of fall colors.

years.src: Tone Glow 143: Lync · Wikipedia: Lync · Suicide Squeeze: These Are Not Fall Colors reissue · Wikipedia: Remembering the Fireballs (Part 8)
years.h: Lync never breaks up, it just stops playing
years.p: The last show is at the Velvet Elvis in Seattle. Wikipedia dates the split to late 1994.
years.xp:
Per Tone Glow, a final tour date with Team Dresch in Eastern Washington came just before it. No one in the sources I found gives a reason for the end. Bertram on the album's release: "It's almost separate from when we were a band. It was after us, in a weird way."

A live recording from Gilman Street in Berkeley, mid-1994, is the last track on Remembering the Fireballs (Part 8).

eras.title: Three bands out of one
eras.text: Bertram forms Red Stars Theory and joins Built to Spill's touring band with Schneider. Jayne goes solo on a four-track and calls it Love as Laughter.

years.src: Wikipedia: Red Stars Theory · Wikipedia: Lync
years.h: Bertram's new band has Modest Mouse's drummer in it
years.p: [[Red Stars Theory|a9d2b2fe-b01c-4115-803c-0514ef05f8ff]] starts in Seattle with [[Jeremiah Green|7c84fd8e-1087-48c6-bd3d-b865819b5306]] on drums and runs through 2000.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, the band made two albums, But Sleep Came Slowly (1997) and Life in a Bubble Can Be Beautiful (1999), on labels including Deluxe, Rx Remedy, Touch and Go and Suicide Squeeze. Green and Bertram both had other bands (Modest Mouse and 764-HERO), which limited how much Red Stars Theory could tour. Wikipedia's Lync article adds that Bertram later co-founded the label and merch company Luckyhorse Industries.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Normal Years · Wikipedia: Lync · Brooklyn Vegan: Lync track-by-track on These Are Not Fall Colors
years.h: Built to Spill's Doug Martsch hires Lync's rhythm section
years.p: Bertram and Schneider tour with [[Built to Spill|3ac482b8-1494-4071-a0e9-f192f9d2c2b0]], and both play on "Some" on The Normal Years, recorded live at Chicago Filmmaker in mid-1995 and released April 30 on K.
years.xp: Brooklyn Vegan reports the album impressed Martsch enough that he recruited Schneider and Bertram as the rhythm section for the There's Nothing Wrong with Love tour. Wikipedia credits Schneider with drums on "Some".

years.src: Stereogum: Love As Laughter's Sam Jayne Dead At 46 · AllMusic: Lync biography · Wikipedia: Love as Laughter · Variety: Sam Jayne, Frontman of Love as Laughter, Dies at 46 · Spin: Sam Jayne and the Plight of Indie Musicians
years.h: Love as Laughter begins in 1994 or 1996, depending on who you ask
years.p: Sam Jayne's four-track project is a full New York band by 1998.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's Love as Laughter article says the project began in 1994, right after Lync; Stereogum and AllMusic say 1996. By 1998, per Stereogum, it was a full band based in New York, and it went on to record for K, Sub Pop and [[Isaac Brock|071d3d16-8ed7-4e06-be96-2c52defcf434]]'s Glacial Pace. Wikipedia says Schneider contributed to the early releases.

Variety reports that Jayne was also briefly a member of [[Modest Mouse|a96ac800-bfcb-412a-8a63-0a98df600700]]; Spin says he played maracas with them on Saturday Night Live in 2004.

years.src: Wikipedia: Remembering the Fireballs (Part 8) · Wikipedia: Lync
years.p: K and Troubleman Unlimited gather 14 tracks of singles and unreleased songs, recorded across 1993 and 1994.
years.xp: Wikipedia's credits split the sources: tracks 1 to 5 recorded by Pat Maley in early 1993, tracks 6 to 12 by Tim Green in late 1993, track 13 at John and Stu's Place in mid-1994, and track 14 live at Gilman in mid-1994. Bertram and Maley are the producers.

eras.title: The record gets a second life
eras.text: Jayne dies in December 2020. Three years later Suicide Squeeze reissues the album.

years.src: Variety: Sam Jayne, Frontman of Love as Laughter, Dies at 46 · Stereogum: Love As Laughter's Sam Jayne Dead At 46 · Spin: Sam Jayne and the Plight of Indie Musicians · Brooklyn Vegan: Sam Jayne of Love as Laughter has died · Wikipedia: Love as Laughter
years.h: Sam Jayne is found dead in New York at 46
years.p: Robin Pecknold of Fleet Foxes on Jayne, as quoted by Brooklyn Vegan. Variety reported he was found in his car; Spin reported his family said the cause was undiagnosed heart conditions.
years.xp:
Stereogum and Spin report he was reported missing on December 6 and found on December 15; Brooklyn Vegan and Variety give December 7 as the last contact. Bandmate Zeke Howard confirmed the news on Instagram. Stereogum reported no signs of foul play.

Spin reported that Jayne had been bartending in Brooklyn, including at Clem's in Williamsburg, where he ran a weekly music-video night, and that during the pandemic he was living between a few places, according to Howard. Fleet Foxes' Robin Pecknold called him "an elusive and formatively inspiring hero," as quoted by Brooklyn Vegan.

years.src: Suicide Squeeze: These Are Not Fall Colors reissue · Wikipedia: These Are Not Fall Colors
years.h: Suicide Squeeze reissues the album as a double LP
years.p: Remastered, with a bonus track ("Can't Tie Yet"), a gatefold, an 18x24 poster and liner notes by Brian Cook.
years.xp: Three vinyl variants: 250 half-and-half copies for the band, 250 twist copies for the label, 1,000 color-in-color for retail. Jesse LeDoux expanded the artwork; Phil Ek's original recording was remastered.
